what: THE ONE PLACE THE PROJECT'S EXPECTED CHECK AND FAILURE COUNTS LIVE. Written at Batch DE. `check_de.gd` reads this after every battery and reports; `docs/state.md` and `CLAUDE.md` POINT AT IT AND DO NOT RESTATE IT, because a second copy of a number is this project's oldest recurring defect.
how_a_row_moves: A BASELINE MOVES ONLY IN THE BATCH THAT CAUSES THE MOVEMENT, AND THE CHANGELOG SAYS WHY. Otherwise the table drifts into whatever the code happens to do.

fields.kind: suite | gate | scene | harness — chooses how the log is parsed.
fields.checks: [lo, hi] expected check count, or null when the target reports no readable count. THE FLOOR IS ASSERTED AND THE CEILING IS NOT: a FALLING count is an error, a RISING one is a notice.
fields.fails: [lo, hi] expected FAILURE count, or null when unreadable. THE POLARITY INVERTS: a RISING failure count is an error (the 48th failure among 47), a FALLING one is a notice.
fields.checks_obs / fails_obs: HOW MANY READINGS THE ROW RESTS ON. A band is a claim about a distribution nobody has characterised and the readings behind it are part of the claim — an's nine-observation band was exceeded on its tenth. THE COUNTING RULE: one per battery reading the record names from DC forward, plus DE's THREE (before on unmodified HEAD, after, and the final acceptance run) = 6, with named exceptions counted low where there is any doubt. A row whose FAILURE evidence differs from its CHECK evidence carries its own number — see test_batch_bo and test_rune_battle.
fields.expect: optional: a verdict substring that must appear, for a target that reports no counts at all.
fields.flake: optional: a KNOWN flake and its observed rate. Its failure count is carried as a band for that reason.
fields.note: optional: why this row is what it is.

check_di.note: NEW AT DI, AND THE ROW IS A RATCHET RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT. §1 counts `_apply_status` call sites out of battle.gd's own text with a BALANCED-PAREN WALK and asserts `src` coverage never falls below the floor the last batch left (DI 99, DJ 106) and that no site passes an explicit `null`. IT WALKS RATHER THAN GREPS BECAUSE THE FIGURE DI INHERITED — 53 of 204, in docs/state.md and in DH's own comment — WAS A GREP AND WAS WRONG: 25 of the 204 calls wrap across lines and twelve of those already passed a source, so real coverage before DI was 63. §2 measures Harvest's ally term on a SEEDED pair (both arms draw the same stream, per DD's rule) and asserts the ratio is 1.5 exactly, with a self-vs-self arm and an enemy-source arm as the negative halves. §3 drives the changed call sites through real casts. §4 ASSERTED THE COMPANION GAP DI FOUND AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT CLOSE, AND DJ RULED ON IT: its third assertion moved from 1.0 (a companion-opened wound paid nothing) to 1.5 (it pays what a hero's pays). THE FIRST TWO DID NOT MOVE — `heroes` still does not hold the companion and `_hero_side()` still does. Count is unchanged at 44 across the ruling, over 10 readings.

check_dj.note: NEW AT DJ. THE GATE FOR “an ally loop reads `companions` too”. §1 reads Harvest's ally loop out of battle.gd's own text and asserts it walks the written-out union `heroes + companions` — NOT `_hero_side()`, which filters `dead` and would silently stop paying for a wound a FALLEN hero opened. §2 measures the payout twice: hand-stamped to a companion (1.5, the same band check_di §2 gives a hero) and on a wound opened by a REAL `_companion_strike` (1.125 — one of four wounds is the ally's), so a site that stops passing its source reds even though the arithmetic still works. §3 drives four of the seven companion call sites live and asserts the other three off the source, and SAYS WHICH IS WHICH. §4 IS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE COLLECTION ITSELF: a fallen hero's wound must still pay 1.0 of a living one — DI's proposed one-word `_hero_side()` fix passes §2 and reads 0.6664 here. §5 ratchets the DJ §2 sweep population so it cannot move in silence — the 23 no-op `is_companion` filters over `heroes`, and the ELEVEN other ally-worded effects each pinned by its own read line. It RULES ON NONE OF IT: a fragment that stops matching is a NOTICE to re-derive DJ §2's table, not a regression. §6 asserts the wrong belief is gone from the four LIVE prose sites, and deliberately does not sweep the changelog or the batch reports, which are history. Gate takes ~4s. COUNTED LOW ON PURPOSE: the gate ran eight times in DJ, but five of those were at 43 checks, BEFORE §5 grew the eleven-site ratchet. Only THREE readings support the 54, and only TWO of those are clean (the third is negative control 5, which reads 54 / 1 by design). A row rests on the readings of the shape it records, not on the batch's total.

check_map.note: ITS `fails` FIGURE IS ITS OWN `reach-contiguity failures: N` LINE, not a suite tally — that is what the battery's grep reads here too, and it is a real number worth ratcheting. Not a hang: ~99% CPU for about five minutes. The battery gives it a 600s bound.

check_map_screen.note: REPORTS NEITHER COUNT NOR FAILURES. Its whole verdict is the one line in `expect`, which is why that line is pinned.

check_parse.note: Walks res://scripts and res://scenes only — it does NOT cover the suites, the gates or the two fixtures. Its verdict is read off stderr, never off a tally: a --script target whose base class does not resolve prints a parse error, runs not one line, and EXITS 0.

test_batch_at.note: FOUND BY THE DG BATTERY DISAGREEING WITH DG'S OWN PREDICTION, AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. The three exclusive-pair reds are DELETED at DG §2 (470 -> 467, part of the sanctioned fall of six); this row's remaining ceiling of 1 is a DIFFERENT and NEW failure. IT IS NOT DG's: DG's only edits to this file were three deleted file-reading assertions, which consume no RNG, and the check count landed exactly on prediction. THE ±10% DAMAGE ROLL ALONE DOES NOT EXPLAIN 2.40 — modelled over 200,000 trials, ten summed casts a side put the 5th-95th percentile at 2.08-2.26 and P(over the 2.35 ceiling) at 0.1%, about one run in a thousand. So there is a SECOND random term. THE SUITE'S OWN `_spawn` NAMES THE CANDIDATE, on the very helper this check calls: 'THE CRIT IS THE THIRD COIN AND ON THIS SPEC IT IS THE WORST ONE: Runaway Resonance adds +1% crit PER STACK, so a same-cast-at-0-vs-12 comparison silently compares 10% crit against 22% crit.' The fixture passes crit:-10.0, which removes the BASE and not the PER-STACK term, so the two populations differ in crit chance as well as in the curve the check means to measure. A model carrying the FULL differential over-predicts (32% red against 1 in 18 observed), so the live term is smaller than that and larger than zero, and ITS SIZE IS NOT ESTABLISHED — do not guess it. THE FIX IS THE DD SHAPE, WHICH DD APPLIED TWICE IN THIS SUITE AND DID NOT REACH THIS ONE: seed both blows of the compared pair, or set crit_bonus back as the file's own comment says checks that care must do. DO NOT WIDEN THE BAND — the band IS the question. DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable, and `bo`'s and `test_rune_battle`'s are both still open.

test_rune_battle.note: FOUND BY `check_de` ON ITS FIRST ACCEPTANCE RUN AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. Its CHECK count is rock steady at 97 across all 15 readings — only the failure moves, which is the flake signature CLAUDE.md names. READINGS: clean in DE's before- and after-batteries, RED in the final acceptance battery, RED on the next ad-hoc run, then TEN CONSECUTIVE CLEAN runs on an idle machine. BOTH REDS LANDED UNDER LOAD, which is a hypothesis and not a finding — the assertion's own comment says the snapshot 'is the one that cannot race', so a race is the thing to look at first. THE FIX IS THE `at`/`bo` SHAPE (seed the draw, or assert on the snapshot alone) AND IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable. SEEDED AT DF §0, per-site: `_seeded()` immediately before the forced hit and nowhere else, so the other 96 checks keep their own stream. THE BAND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED — two clean post-seed readings cannot retire a rate measured over fifteen, and tightening on that evidence is the same fault as writing a band from too few readings, in the opposite direction. The failure message now carries the state the forced hit happened in (battle_over, both units' liveness, the target's fire resist, the pierce fraction), so the NEXT red says what was missing instead of only that it was missing.
